frontend.router: @angular/router (standalone, hash routing on the demo host)

backend.note: the frontend talks to a hosted RealWorld API at https://api.realworld.show/api (src/app/core/interceptors/api.interceptor.ts:4). There is no backend source to read.

apiDocs.note: the RealWorld API is specified publicly, but nothing in this clone documents it; endpoints here are read from the Angular services (Tier C).

notes: The demo host serves plain path routes (/login), matching the route table. An earlier reading assumed a hash fragment; the crawl's own URLs settled it.
Routes are lazy (loadComponent/loadChildren), so the component of a route is an import path rather than a class reference — recorded as the module path.

regions.name: ArticleList
regions.note: Not a <table>: the feed is a list of article cards. It is still a collection — rows addressed by the article title they contain.

labelAssociation.note: There are no <label> elements at all: every input carries only a placeholder. getByLabel is unusable; getByPlaceholder is the app's real vocabulary, and formControlName is the stable identifier behind it.

notes: The feed is a card list, not a table, which is why the collection convention names app-article-preview as its row. A collection does not have to be a <table>.

auth.scheme: JWT in an Authorization: Token <jwt> header

users.note: the demo allows self-registration via POST /api/users, so a test user is created rather than shared. This is the only corpus app where a test can make its own account.

authVerification.reason: APP_USERNAME / APP_PASSWORD are not set in the environment

endpoints.summary: create an article — the precondition workhorse
delete an article — use for cleanup

notes: Every row is Tier C: this clone contains no backend and no specification, so these endpoints are what the Angular services call, not what the server promises. The RealWorld API is specified publicly — if a precondition needs a guarantee, read that spec rather than trusting this file.
The API is shared and world-writable. Create what you assert on.
